newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya's Gaddafi says he has support for Arab summit.
newsitem.headline: Libya's Gaddafi says he has support for Arab summit.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi said on Wednesday all Arab heads of state welcomed his call for an Arab summit.
Gaddafi's envoys toured Arab states at the end of May and early in June to invite leaders to a summit intended to discuss what Tripoli called challenges of the next century for the Arabs.
"All the responses were positive. All Arab rulers agreed to hold an Arab summit," the Libyan leader said in a speech broadcast live by the Libyan state-run television, monitored in Tunis.
Gaddafi, speaking at a rally in the eastern coastal city of Derna, did not say when the summit would take place or where.
Last week diplomats in Kuwait said Gulf states had turned down the call.

Arab leaders last met in Egypt in June 1996 to discuss the Middle East peace process after Benjamin Netanyahu was elected Israeli prime minister. In late April Egypt said it opposed convening an Arab summit for fear it could complicate the stalled peace process.
"The Arab heads of state feel there is need for a summit now...particularly that Netanyahu rejected the Arab efforts for peace and proclaimed that Arabs must surrender," Gaddafi said.

"The Arabs also had been having some hope with the Israeli Labour (party)...It is now led by a fascist leader," Gaddafi said in an apparent reference to Israeli general Ehud Barak, who was elected last week as Labour leader.
